key_insight: Deep-network Poisson intensity estimators admit Hellinger-risk guarantees even when true intensities vanish, with improved convergence rates under compositional or low-dimensional manifold structure.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports flexible event-rate modeling from observed covariates, including neural spiking applications where rates may approach zero.
method: Estimate covariate-dependent intensities using nonparametric maximum likelihood.
Derive an oracle inequality for covariate-averaged Hellinger distance without a positive lower bound on intensity.
Apply the bound to deep neural networks, obtaining nearly minimax-optimal rates for compositional intensities and adaptation to manifold structure.
evidence_signal: Simulations favor DNN estimators over kernels in most settings, and Allen Brain Observatory neural-spiking data show better held-out log-likelihood than a conditional kernel estimator.
watch_item: DNN estimators are not uniformly superior: manifold kernels remain competitive in some simulation designs.
paper_title: Nonparametric Intensity Estimation for Covariate-Driven Poisson Processes Using Deep Learning
